preconditions.description: The number of junctions n is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(s) == n and all(-10000 <= x <= 10000 for x in s)
preconditions.description: The list s contains exactly n integers, each between -10,000 and 10,000 inclusive.
The number of pipes m is between 0 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in pipes)
preconditions.description: Each pipe connects two distinct junctions within the valid range [1, n].
The list of pipes contains exactly m entries.

preconditions.expression: len(set(tuple(sorted(p)) for p in pipes)) == m
preconditions.description: No unordered pair of junctions appears more than once in the input.
The graph formed by the pipes is connected (guaranteed by the problem statement).

postconditions.description: A solution exists if and only if the sum of all junction constraints s_i is zero.
If no solution exists, the output is exactly 'Impossible'.

postconditions.expression: is_possible and stdout_lines[0] == 'Possible' and len(stdout_lines) == m + 1
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the first line is 'Possible' followed by exactly m lines.

postconditions.expression: is_possible and all(-2000000000 <= int(f) <= 2000000000 for f in stdout_lines[1:])
postconditions.description: Each pipe setting f_i is an integer within the range [-2*10^9, 2*10^9].

postconditions.expression: is_possible and all(sum((f if u == x else (-f if v == x else 0)) for i, (u, v) in enumerate(pipes) for f in [int(stdout_lines[i+1])]) == s[x-1] for x in range(1, n+1))
postconditions.description: For every junction x, the net flow (incoming minus outgoing) equals s_x, where flow on pipe i is f_i from x_i to y_i.
